what_it_does: RowHammer is a known attack where repeatedly reading the same row of memory (DRAM — a common type of computer memory chip) causes bits in neighboring rows to flip, corrupting data. Chip makers have added defenses that, when they detect suspicious repeated reads, pause normal memory access and run protective refresh operations. This paper shows that those very defenses create a new problem: the pause itself is measurable and leaks information. A spy program can watch how long memory accesses take and infer what a victim program is doing — or two programs can deliberately use these pauses to send secret messages to each other through a channel the operating system cannot see. The paper names this class of attack LeakyHammer, builds two concrete examples, demonstrates it can identify which websites a user is browsing, and evaluates three fixes.
